
```json
[
  {
    "id": "TC-001",
    "title": "Verify display of patient pressure at the gas outlet port",
    "req_ids": ["RW-SW-46"],
    "kind": "positive",
    "preconditions": ["Gas outlet port data is available from the controller"],
    "inputs": {"controllerData": "Patient pressure data"},
    "steps": [
      "Navigate to the patient pressure display section",
      "Input the patient pressure data from the controller",
      "Assert that the displayed pressure matches the input data"
    ],
    "expected": ["The displayed patient pressure matches the controller data"]
  },
  {
    "id": "TC-002",
    "title": "Verify graph refresh rate is at least 20 Hz",
    "req_ids": ["RW-SW-47"],
    "kind": "positive",
    "preconditions": ["GUI is operational"],
    "inputs": {},
    "steps": [
      "Observe the graph refresh rate",
      "Input a trigger to refresh the graph multiple times",
      "Count the number of refreshes within a fixed time interval"
    ],
    "expected": ["The graph refreshes at least 5 times within the interval, indicating a refresh rate of >= 20 Hz"]
  },
  {
    "id": "TC-003",
    "title": "Verify graph duration is 30 seconds",
    "req_ids": ["RW-SW-48"],
    "kind": "positive",
    "preconditions": ["Graph has been displayed for at least 30 seconds"],
    "inputs": {},
    "steps": [
      "Start a timer",
      "Keep the graph displayed for 30 seconds",
      "Assert that the timer has reached 30 seconds"
    ],
    "expected": ["The timer confirms a display duration of 30 seconds"]
  },
  {
    "id": "TC-004",
    "title": "Verify inspiratory tidal volume range and resolution",
    "req_ids": ["RW-SW-50"],
    "kind": "positive",
    "preconditions": ["Graph is displaying tidal volume data"],
    "inputs": {"inspiratoryTidalVolume": "0..1000mL", "expiratoryTidalVolume": "0..1000mL"},
    "steps": [
      "Input the inspiratory and expiratory tidal volume values",
      "Assert that the inspiratory volume is within 0..1000mL and the ratio is within 10:1 to 1:200 with the specified resolution",
      "Check the transition from inspire to expire is after the plateau phase"
    ],
    "expected": ["The inspiratory volume is within range and the ratio is as specified, with correct transition after plateau"]
  },
  {
    "id": "TC-005",
    "title": "Verify PEEP display increments of 1 cmH2O",
    "req_ids": ["RW-SW-53"],
    "kind": "positive",
    "preconditions": ["PEEP data is available"],
    "inputs": {"PEEPValue": "1 cmH2O"},
    "steps": [
      "Input the PEEP value",
      "Assert that the displayed value is in increments of 1 cmH2O"
    ],
    "expected": ["The displayed PEEP value is in increments of 1 cmH2O"]
  },
  {
    "id": "TC-006",
    "title": "Verify volume provided to the patient graph",
    "req_ids": ["RW-SW-54"],
    "kind": "positive",
    "preconditions": ["Graph of volume provided is active"],
    "inputs": {},
    "steps": [
      "Observe the volume provided graph",
      "Assert that the graph shows the volume provided over the last 30 seconds",
      "Check the graph's refresh rate and duration"
    ],
    "expected": ["The graph refreshes at >= 20 Hz and has a duration of 30 seconds, displaying the volume provided accurately"
    }
]
```

Note: The above JSON test cases are written in a simplified format for illustrative purposes. In practice, the "steps" would involve more detailed actions to simulate user interactions with the GUI, and the "expected" outcomes would be more specific assertions that can be programmatically checked. The "preconditions" would also include any setup or state changes required before each test case. The actual GUI Event Graphs notation would visually represent these steps and expected outcomes, which is not possible to convey in plain text format here. However, the JSON structure provides a clear and executable test suite that can be translated into a visual GUI Event Graphs artifact for scoring.
